sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Delaware
sections.html:
Property tax here is billed locally by county tax offices, and the rate you pay depends mostly on your school district. In Kent County, the tax is the taxable value multiplied by the rate, with the school district setting most of that rate and the county government and county library adding to it.

Two houses of equal value can get different bills, even inside one county. A home in the Colonial school district in New Castle County is billed on different rates than one in Appoquinimink. Read the bill for your own parcel and the district printed on it, not a neighbor's number.

With only three counties, the structure is easy to hold in your head.

  • New Castle County: the northern county, with five school districts that lie entirely within it plus a vocational-technical district.
  • Kent County: the middle county, billed by the Kent County Receiver of Taxes.
  • Sussex County: the southern county, billed through the Sussex County Treasury and Billing offices in Georgetown.

A court ordered Delaware to reassess after decades without new values. New Castle and Kent counties had not reassessed since the 1980s and Sussex had not done so since 1974, and a 2020 Court of Chancery ruling followed a 2018 lawsuit over the old system.

House Bill 62 now requires each county to reassess every five years. Kent County's current values are as of July 1, 2023, and New Castle County's are as of July 1, 2024.

The reassessment matters to a seller in two ways. Your assessed value now tracks market value much more closely, so a buyer reading your bill sees a number tied to a recent date. And exemptions and abatements were not built into the new assessed values. They are applied once a rate is set. Roughly a third of owners saw lower taxes, a third higher and a third about the same. A sale does not trigger a reassessment in Kent County.

In Kent and Sussex counties the annual bill is due September 30. New Castle County's tax code sets a July 1 due date with a penalty that starts after September 1, so New Castle owners should check their own bill for the exact deadline.

A missing bill does not cancel a penalty. Sussex County's tax office says the owner must pay on time even if the bill never arrived, and New Castle's code says the same: not receiving a statement does not excuse timely payment.

New Castle's code also requires the Office of Finance to send at least one written demand for unpaid taxes by December 15 each year. A residential owner with a primary residence and a bill at least $300 above the prior year can qualify for a payment plan of at least three equal school-tax installments.

New Castle County has five districts that lie entirely within the county plus a vocational-technical district, and each sets its own rate. Recently the districts split their rates so that homes are charged a lower rate than apartments, commercial and industrial property. Overpayments of more than $50 can be refunded or credited when bills are recalculated.

To estimate a school bill, divide the assessment by 100 and multiply by the residential rate for your district. Rates are set after school boards vote each summer and change from year to year, so use the rate printed on your current bill instead of a number from an old article.

sections.h2: Exemptions and credits that lower a bill
sections.html:
Delaware offers a school tax credit for seniors, a county exemption for low-income seniors and the disabled, and full exemptions for government, school, religious and some charitable property. Most require an application, and most have a spring deadline.

  • Senior School Property Tax Credit: the owner must be 65 or older and the property must be the primary residence. Applications are due April 30. Residency rules depend on when you became a Delaware domiciliary: before 2013, no waiting period beyond eligibility in the following tax year; from 2013 through 2017, three consecutive years; from January 1, 2018, ten consecutive years. The bill must be paid in full by the end of the tax year. Confirm the current cap with your county before relying on a figure.
  • Kent County senior and disability exemption: age 65 by May 31 or total disability, income limits of $18,000 for one applicant or $24,750 combined with a spouse, and yearly reapplication by April 30. Title must be in the applicant's name.
  • General exemptions: government property, school property used for education, religious property not held as an investment, certain charitable property and parkland owned by civic groups such as homeowners' associations.

Sussex County sends applications for its senior, disability and State 65 exemptions through the Billing Office at (302) 855-7871.

Appeal in writing to your county, and treat the deadlines as firm. In Kent County an annual appeal must reach the Assessment Office by 5:00 p.m. on January 31 to affect the tax year beginning June 1, and a postmark does not count. Appeals of quarterly supplemental increases must be filed within 30 days of notice. Deadlines can shift in reassessment years. For New Castle County, the Board of Assessment Review deadline is March 15.

During a reassessment there is also an informal review with the contractor, Tyler Technologies, before the formal county appeal.

Look at refund rules before you sell. Kent County's refund policy follows state law and covers limited cases, such as tax paid while an appeal is pending or a duplicate bill. An error found after the appeal window usually does not produce a refund, because Delaware law puts the burden of making sure assessment data is accurate on the property owner.

An appeal still open at closing is a loose end. Tell the title company about it so the proceeds and any refund are handled in writing.

sections.h2: Selling a Delaware house with property tax due
sections.html:
Unpaid property tax is collected out of the sale or, if it stays unpaid long enough, through a court-supervised tax sale. Expect the title company to find the balance and pay it from proceeds at closing.

Under the monition method in the Delaware Code, the tax collector files in Superior Court, the sheriff posts a notice on the property, and the notice gives 20 days to pay before the tax authority can ask for a sale. After a tax sale the owner has 60 days after court approval to redeem by paying the purchaser the price plus 15 percent and costs. Kent County's sheriff procedures describe tax sales about every three months, with the full bid due the same day.

If you owe, work through this list.

  • Pull the current bill and any supplemental bills from the county tax portal.
  • Check whether a mortgage escrow already paid it. Sussex County offers an EscrowCheck tool and forwards bills to mortgage companies.
  • After closing, report the ownership change to the county assessment office. Sussex lists (302) 855-7824 for ownership changes.
  • Keep proof of payment for any exemption you are leaving behind.

A cash buyer who takes the house as-is can close with the tax balance paid from proceeds, often the simplest route when back taxes are growing by the month. Any figure depends on the county records for your parcel.

faqs.q: Does Delaware have a state property tax?
faqs.a: Property tax is billed by counties and school districts. Your bill comes from the county tax office and reflects your school district's rate.

faqs.q: When is the Delaware property tax due date?
faqs.a: Kent and Sussex counties list September 30 for the annual bill. New Castle County's code sets July 1 with penalties after September 1, so check the due date printed on your New Castle bill.

faqs.q: Will selling my house trigger a new assessment?
faqs.a: Not in Kent County, where a sale does not trigger reassessment. Values change only for a countywide reassessment, a change to the property or a corrected error. Delaware counties now reassess every five years.

faqs.q: Can seniors reduce Delaware property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The state Senior School Property Tax Credit covers homeowners 65 and older on their primary residence, with an April 30 application deadline. Kent County also has an income-limited senior and disability exemption.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Delaware house to a cash buyer if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, in many cases. The tax balance is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the title company confirms the payoff with the county. The earlier you sell, the less penalty builds up.
